correctness.rationale: The Catalan constant term is the central binomial coefficient minus its neighbor; binomial transformation gives CT((1−z)(z⁻¹+1+z)^n). As a check on the recurrence normalization, its ordinary generating function from that transform is F=(1−sqrt((1−3x)/(1+x)))/(2x), which satisfies x(1−2x−3x²)F′+(1−3x²)F=1 and F(0)=1. For N=p^r, coefficientwise Frobenius yields R_N≡1 and R_(N−1)≡k_N mod p, where k_0=0 and k_m=−2 for m≡2 mod 3 and 1 otherwise for m>0. The recurrence denominator N+2 is a unit at every odd p. The bracket is 5 or −4 mod p, so only p=5 and even r require further work. Raising congruent Laurent polynomials mod 5 to the fifth power proves the mod-25 reduction to T(z^(5^(r−1)))^5. The coefficients 51,45,30,15,5,1 give bracket 15 mod 25 for even r, exactly one extra factor of five. This works for all even r≥2; p=3 and r=1 require no exceptional assumption. Independent modular counts of Motzkin paths with level-zero horizontals forbidden reproduced 21 valuations over seven odd primes, including 5²+1 and 5⁴+1. The all-exponent proof is not inferred from these counts.
residual_risks: The proof gives no claim for p=2 or general indices; the unit denominator is needed.

A005043 points to the thesis The Automatic Study of Constant Term Sequences Modulo Prime Powers, pp. 116–117; a redirect prevented access to those pages.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Fixed-prime methods may encode slices, including some 3-adic cases. The inspected results do not supply a uniform odd-prime noncancellation test or the exceptional 5-adic parity calculation.

value.rationale: These indices arise at the prime-power recurrence numerator, not from an arbitrary modulus sweep. Distinguishing a unit bracket from exact first-order cancellation at five provides a sharp classification, including an infinite exceptional branch invisible to mod-p testing alone.
residual_risks: Value is for this complete index family, not for a general new congruence algorithm or broader claims about Riordan valuations.
